radiology_report:
Tergooi MC
Department of Radiology
Date: 15 January 2025
Exam: Multiparametric MRI prostate

Clinical indication: Rising PSA to 8.2 ng/mL, prior Gleason 3+3 diagnosis. Evaluation for dominant clinical lesion.

FINDINGS:
The prostate measures 66.0 mL. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal area of low signal intensity within the mid-peripheral zone, extending bilaterally. On diffusion-weighted imaging, this region shows restricted diffusion with corresponding low apparent diffusion coefficient values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences reveal early focal enhancement in the same location. The lesion measures approximately 14 mm in maximum dimension. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is visualized.

IMPRESSION:
Suspicious focal lesion in the mid-peripheral zone, bilateral extension.
PI-RADS v2.1 score: 4.
Prostate-specific antigen density: 0.12 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage: cT2a.
csPCa predicted probability 0.74084973.

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with a PSA of 4.2 ng/mL, elevated from baseline. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable at this time. Given the rising PSA trend, a multiparametric MRI was arranged, followed by a transperineal biopsy which confirmed ISUP grade group 1 prostate cancer. The patient was counselled regarding active surveillance and agreed to proceed with regular monitoring.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1, 16 February 2024:
Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. The tumour exhibits an acinar growth pattern. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. Perineural invasion is absent. The tumour is located in the mid-prostate, bilateral.

Biopsy 2, 20 January 2025:
Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. The tumour exhibits an acinar growth pattern. No cribriform or intraductal patterns identified. Perineural invasion is absent. The tumour is located in the mid-prostate, bilateral.

Summary: The histological findings across both biopsy timepoints remain stable at ISUP grade group 1 with consistent acinar growth and no high-risk features.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 3.
